chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A man came to him at night and said, 'May Allah improve you. A woman with us has menstruated and has not performed the Tawaf of the women.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I have been asked about this matter today.' The man said, 'May Allah improve you, I am her husband, and I would like to hear that from you.' He (peace be upon him) fell silent as if he were conversing with himself, and he said, 'Her beauty will not remain upon her, and she is not able to stay behind from her companions. She can go, and her Hajj is complete.'

key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf of the women, a specific circumambulation performed by women after their menstruation ends

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who misses Tawaf al-Nisa due to menstruation during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical dilemma of a woman who missed Tawaf al-Nisa' due to menstruation, ruling that her Hajj remains valid and she may depart with her companions. The Imam’s pause and remark regarding her 'beauty' (jamal) reflect the Shia scholarly view that the ritual obligation is fulfilled despite the delay, emphasizing ease in religious practice. This highlights the principle that Hajj is not invalidated by the inability to perform a specific post-Hajj ritual at the exact moment, provided the core rites are completed.
